summary.one_liner: Research code implementing the "Improving Factuality and Reasoning in Language Models through Multiagent Debate" paper, where several LLM agents debate answers over rounds on math, GSM, biography, and MMLU tasks.
summary.what_it_does: The repository is a preliminary implementation of the multiagent debate method from a 2023 paper by Du, Li, Torralba, Tenenbaum, and Mordatch. Each task lives in its own subfolder: math, gsm, biography, and mmlu. Each folder has a generation script that produces debate-based answers and an evaluation script that scores them. The README says more tasks and settings will be released later and links to some additional debate logs. It does not describe the model backends, prompt details, or number of agents or rounds beyond the paper's method.
use_cases: reproduce multiagent debate results from the paper
evaluate LLM factuality on biography generation
run arithmetic and math word problems through multi-agent LLM debate
benchmark debate-style answers on GSM and MMLU
study how multiple language model agents improve reasoning
notable: Implements the multiagent debate method from the arXiv 2305.14325 paper
Separate generate and evaluate scripts for math, GSM, biography, and MMLU tasks
Points to a community implementation using open-source LLMs by gauss5930
caveats: Described by the author as a preliminary implementation
README says more tasks and settings will be released soon, so coverage is limited
README does not list dependencies, required API keys, or model setup
